source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PO.1 Define Security Requirements for Software Development
proposed_assessment_use: Check whether security requirements are explicit, maintained, communicated, and carried through the SDLC.
suggested_evidence: Requirements records; architecture/security criteria; exception records; third-party requirements.
adaptation_limit: SSDF recommends secure-development practices; it does not prove local implementation or effectiveness.
maturity_handling: Do not convert PO.1 presence/absence directly into a maturity score.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PO.2 Implement Roles and Responsibilities
proposed_assessment_use: Assess whether secure-development responsibilities, ownership, and supporting roles are defined and operationalized.
suggested_evidence: Role descriptions; RACI/ownership records; training records; review/escalation paths.
adaptation_limit: Role documentation alone is not evidence that responsibilities are executed consistently.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

proposed_assessment_use: Assess how toolchains support repeatable secure development, build, test, release, and evidence capture.
suggested_evidence: CI/CD configuration; tool inventory; access controls; scan/test logs; provenance records.
adaptation_limit: Tool presence is not equivalent to process quality or secure outcomes.
maturity_handling: Evaluate evidence of use and control effectiveness separately from any local maturity rubric.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PO.4 Define and Use Criteria for Software Security Checks
proposed_assessment_use: Assess whether security gates/check criteria are defined, risk-based, and used consistently before release.
suggested_evidence: Definition-of-done; merge/release gates; exception approvals; test criteria; failure handling.
adaptation_limit: SSDF does not prescribe one universal gate set or numeric threshold.
maturity_handling: Any rating must be locally defined and evidence-based, not labeled an SSDF score.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PO.5 Implement and Maintain Secure Environments for Software Development
proposed_assessment_use: Assess isolation, access control, change control, and maintenance of development/build environments.
suggested_evidence: Environment diagrams; privileged-access records; configuration baselines; patch/change records.
adaptation_limit: Environment design must be interpreted in local threat and operating context.
maturity_handling: No maturity level is supplied by SSDF.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PS.1 Protect All Forms of Code from Unauthorized Access and Tampering
proposed_assessment_use: Assess protection of source, build artifacts, configuration, and related software assets.
suggested_evidence: Repository permissions; branch protections; artifact controls; audit logs; secret handling.
adaptation_limit: Protection controls should be evaluated for actual scope and enforcement, not policy text alone.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PS.2 Provide a Mechanism for Verifying Software Release Integrity
proposed_assessment_use: Assess whether releases can be verified as authentic and unchanged from approved build outputs.
suggested_evidence: Signing/provenance evidence; checksums; release metadata; deployment verification records.
adaptation_limit: The specific mechanism is implementation-dependent; do not infer a required vendor or architecture.
maturity_handling: Use evidence of repeatability and coverage; do not call it an SSDF maturity tier.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PS.3 Archive and Protect Each Software Release
proposed_assessment_use: Assess reproducibility, custody, and retention of released software and release metadata.
suggested_evidence: Artifact repository; retention policy; release manifests; restore/rebuild evidence.
adaptation_limit: Retention duration and mechanisms are context-dependent.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PW.1 Design Software to Meet Security Requirements and Mitigate Security Risks
proposed_assessment_use: Assess whether threat/risk considerations and security requirements shape design decisions.
suggested_evidence: Threat/risk models; design records; security requirements; architecture decisions; exception rationale.
adaptation_limit: A documented design artifact does not prove resulting software is secure.
maturity_handling: Treat observed practice and outcome evidence separately from any locally proposed scale.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PW.2 Review the Software Design to Verify Compliance with Security Requirements and Risk Information
proposed_assessment_use: Assess design review independence, coverage, traceability, and response to findings.
suggested_evidence: Review records; sign-offs; issue tracking; traceability to requirements and risks.
adaptation_limit: Review quality and depth must be evidenced; review existence alone is insufficient.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PW.4 Reuse Existing, Well-Secured Software When Feasible
proposed_assessment_use: Assess component selection, provenance, maintenance, and risk evaluation for reused software.
suggested_evidence: Dependency inventory/SBOM where available; approval criteria; vulnerability/remediation records.
adaptation_limit: SSDF does not make reuse categorically safer; context and ongoing maintenance matter.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PW.5 Create Source Code by Adhering to Secure Coding Practices
proposed_assessment_use: Assess whether secure coding expectations are defined, taught, reviewed, and evidenced in implementation.
suggested_evidence: Standards; training; code review evidence; static-analysis findings; defect history.
adaptation_limit: Coding standards and tooling are inputs, not proof of secure outcomes.
maturity_handling: Do not translate tool counts or rule coverage into maturity without a separate validated method.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PW.6 Configure the Compilation, Interpreter, and Build Processes to Improve Executable Security
proposed_assessment_use: Assess secure build configuration and repeatability.
suggested_evidence: Build definitions; compiler/interpreter settings; build logs; artifact provenance.
adaptation_limit: Applicability varies by language/platform; not every example applies to every service.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PW.7 Review and/or Analyze Human-Readable Code to Identify Vulnerabilities and Verify Compliance with Security Requirements
proposed_assessment_use: Assess code review and static-analysis coverage, triage, remediation, and exception handling.
suggested_evidence: Review rules; static-analysis results; defect records; remediation SLAs/records.
adaptation_limit: Tool output requires context, validation, and disposition; raw finding counts are not maturity.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PW.8 Test Executable Code to Identify Vulnerabilities and Verify Compliance with Security Requirements
proposed_assessment_use: Assess security-relevant testing of executable software and handling of results.
suggested_evidence: Dynamic/security test records; test environments; findings; retest/closure evidence.
adaptation_limit: Testing depth and relevance depend on system risk and architecture.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / PW.9 Configure Software to Have Secure Settings by Default
proposed_assessment_use: Assess default configuration, deployment hardening, and documentation of security-relevant settings.
suggested_evidence: Configuration baselines; deployment templates; hardening guides; exception records.
adaptation_limit: Secure defaults are context-sensitive and do not replace operational controls.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / RV.1 Identify and Confirm Vulnerabilities on an Ongoing Basis
proposed_assessment_use: Assess intake, validation, monitoring, and confirmation of vulnerabilities after release.
suggested_evidence: Vulnerability intake; scanner results; advisories; validation records; disclosure channels.
adaptation_limit: Finding volume alone is not a maturity or performance metric.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / RV.2 Assess, Prioritize, and Remediate Vulnerabilities
proposed_assessment_use: Assess risk-based prioritization, remediation, verification, and exception handling.
suggested_evidence: Triage criteria; remediation records; patch/release evidence; accepted-risk records.
adaptation_limit: Elapsed time should be interpreted against severity, exposure, service constraints, and policy.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Table 1 / RV.3 Analyze Vulnerabilities to Identify Their Root Causes
proposed_assessment_use: Assess whether significant vulnerabilities produce learning and preventive changes.
suggested_evidence: Root-cause reviews; recurring-defect analysis; coding/design/process changes; retrospectives.
adaptation_limit: Root-cause analysis quality requires evidence; a completed form is not proof of learning.
maturity_handling: No SSDF maturity scale is defined.

source_section_or_element: Section 2 / GOVERN (GV); Appendix A GV.OC, GV.RM, GV.RR, GV.PO, GV.OV, GV.SC
rfq_assessment_area: software development; security; deployment/operations; AI readiness
proposed_assessment_use: Use governance outcomes to examine mission context, risk strategy, roles, policy, oversight, and supply-chain risk around the assessed services.
suggested_evidence: Risk strategy; policy; ownership; oversight records; supplier/service governance evidence.
adaptation_limit: CSF outcomes are not a checklist and do not prescribe how outcomes must be achieved.
maturity_handling: CSF 2.0 Tiers characterize rigor at an organizational level; do not use them as a validated service-level maturity scale.

proposed_assessment_use: Assess whether relevant data, software, services, platforms, dependencies, and suppliers are known sufficiently for risk decisions.
suggested_evidence: Asset/service inventories; dependency maps; ownership records; supplier inventories.
adaptation_limit: Inventory completeness expectations should be risk- and scope-based.
maturity_handling: Do not infer maturity from inventory count or tool adoption.

proposed_assessment_use: Assess how threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact, and risk information inform priorities.
suggested_evidence: Risk assessments; threat/vulnerability inputs; decision records; accepted-risk records.
adaptation_limit: CSF provides outcomes, not a prescribed risk formula.
maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

rfq_assessment_area: software development; security; deployment/operations; AI readiness

proposed_assessment_use: Assess identity/access governance for applications, platforms, administrative paths, and supporting services.
suggested_evidence: IAM architecture; access reviews; joiner/mover/leaver evidence; privileged access records; authentication policies.
adaptation_limit: Specific technical mechanisms depend on risk and architecture.
maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

adaptation_limit: Do not treat public policy statements as proof of implementation within ESS/RIS/IAM.
maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

proposed_assessment_use: Assess configuration, maintenance, software integrity, logging, and protection of platforms supporting services.

adaptation_limit: Platform outcomes do not dictate one implementation stack.
maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

source_section_or_element: Appendix A / PR.IR Technology Infrastructure Resilience

suggested_evidence: Redundancy/failover records; capacity/resilience tests; dependency diagrams; continuity evidence.

maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

source_section_or_element: Appendix A / DE.AE Adverse Event Analysis
proposed_assessment_use: Assess whether detected events are analyzed, correlated, prioritized, and communicated for action.
suggested_evidence: Triage procedures; event records; correlation/analysis evidence; escalation decisions.
adaptation_limit: Event volume and alert closure counts need denominator/context before comparison.
maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

proposed_assessment_use: Assess incident activation, prioritization, handling, and coordination.
suggested_evidence: Incident plans; case records; severity criteria; roles; after-action records.
adaptation_limit: Incident frequency alone is not evidence of poor or strong capability.
maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

proposed_assessment_use: Assess analysis depth, evidence preservation, understanding of impact/root cause, and iterative response.
suggested_evidence: Investigation records; timelines; forensic/diagnostic evidence; root-cause analysis.
adaptation_limit: Depth should be risk-proportionate; not every event requires identical treatment.
maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

proposed_assessment_use: Assess containment and mitigation decision-making and execution.
suggested_evidence: Containment actions; mitigation records; change approvals; validation/recovery evidence.
adaptation_limit: Specific containment techniques are architecture-dependent.
maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

source_section_or_element: Appendix A / RC.RP Incident Recovery Plan Execution
proposed_assessment_use: Assess recovery execution, restoration priorities, validation, and return to normal operations.
suggested_evidence: Recovery plans; exercise/test results; restore logs; service validation; lessons learned.
adaptation_limit: Recovery objectives need local business/service context.
maturity_handling: No validated maturity score is provided by this category.

source_section_or_element: Section 3 and Appendix B / CSF Tiers
rfq_assessment_area: software development; security; deployment/operations; AI readiness
proposed_assessment_use: Use only as optional context for conversations about organizational risk-governance rigor and consistency.
suggested_evidence: Documented governance practices; risk processes; cross-organizational consistency evidence.
adaptation_limit: Appendix B explicitly calls the Tier table a notional illustration; Tiers characterize organizational cyber risk governance and management, not the four Iowa service-area maturity levels.
maturity_handling: Do not import Tier 1-4 as the assessment's maturity scale or as an empirical benchmark.
